questions.say_example: This appeal needs either tracking info or proof of a refund you already gave. Do you actually have one of those on hand? An appeal without it gets denied on arrival.

questions.question: How did you issue the refund?
questions.why: The screen requires you to specify whether the refund was issued through PayPal or another method to ensure the dispute is processed correctly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to accurately report your specific refund method, which could lead to the dispute being mishandled if the agent guesses incorrectly.
questions.check: Does the page ask whether the refund was issued through PayPal or another method?
questions.say_example: Selected <refunded through PayPal>

questions.question: Where do you go to find and close an existing dispute?
questions.why: The screen displays a 'Resolution Centre' card specifically designed to resolve transaction or account issues.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to properly manage and close their existing disputes if the agent navigates to the wrong section.
questions.check: Does the page show a Resolution Centre entry point for managing disputes?
questions.say_example: Opened <Resolution Centre> to find the case

questions.question: Am I sure I want to permanently close this case, knowing I cannot reopen it?
questions.why: The warning modal explicitly states that once the case is closed, you cannot report another issue on this transaction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether they are truly ready to permanently forfeit their right to dispute this specific transaction.
questions.verify_form: The agent faced the close-case warning - check whether it closed; once closed, this transaction can never be disputed again.
questions.check: Does the warning modal state that closing this case is permanent and it cannot be reopened?
questions.say_example: Closing this case is permanent. You can't dispute this transaction again afterward. Still want to close it?

questions.question: Are there any open cases in your queue that you can close?
questions.why: The Resolution Centre displays '0 Open cases' and states there are no cases in your queue, indicating no active disputes are currently available to manage or close.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to personally verify the status of your open cases and manually close any resolved disputes.
questions.check: Does the Resolution Centre show 0 open cases in the queue?
questions.say_example: Resolution Centre shows <0> open cases

questions.question: Does the page show the case marked resolved and closed with a confirmation checkmark?
questions.why: The green checkmark and closure message confirm that the system successfully processed the end of the dispute.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the immediate peace of mind that comes from seeing the final visual confirmation that their dispute is officially closed.
questions.check: Does the page show a checkmark and message confirming the case is marked resolved and closed?
questions.say_example: Case shows <resolved and closed> with a confirmation checkmark

questions.question: How do you report another issue for a transaction that already has a closed case?
questions.why: The screen shows the initial case is already closed with a refund issued, so you must find the specific option to open a new dispute for the same transaction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to ensure all separate issues with a multi-item transaction are fully addressed and refunded.
questions.check: Does the transaction show a closed case with a refund already issued, alongside an option to open a new dispute?
questions.say_example: This transaction has a closed case with a refund already issued - opened a new dispute for the separate issue

children.label: Prevent the next mistake
children.note: 9.1 or 9.2 before the next send; 9.3 where the platform sells refund insurance
